newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares up 1.71 pct as investors skip Wall St.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares up 1.71 pct as investors skip Wall St.

text.p: The Lima Stock Exchange finished up 1.71 percent Wednesday, stoked by good news that lured in foreign investors seeking refuge from a cheerless Wall Street amid high Latin American returns, traders and analysts said.
Analysts were optimistic that Lima stocks will be able to sustain their gains Thursday, but cautioned that there will probably be some selective profit-taking.
"The good prospects for zinc prices, companies' agreements for dividend payments, the good outlook for macroeconomic figures. It's all good news," said Manuel Torres of Finvest.

He singled out mining stock Compania de Minas Buenaventura, which won a court case against BRGM of France for the right to a preferential option to buy BRGM's 24.7 percent stake in gold play Yanacocha.
Buenaventura's common stock rose 4.67 percent to 22.19 soles.
The General Index rose 1.71 percent to 1,624.91 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index gained 1.09 percent to 2,315.01.
In a total of 2,176 trades, volume was estimated at 37.7 million soles ($14.3 million) as 57 stocks rose, 25 were stable and 11 fell.
The biggest rises were polimetallic mining firms Milpo, up 8.82 percent to 18.50 soles, Morococha, up 5.98 percent to 1.95 soles, and Perubar, which climbed 5.34 percent to 3.55 soles.
Losers included Consorcio Fabril Pacifico, slipping 3.05 percent to 4.45 soles, and Cervesur, which lost 2.22 percent to 1.32 soles.
Benchmark Telefonica del Peru B closed unchanged at 5.89 soles, with 1.65 million shares, or 26 percent of total trade, changing hands.

"Everyone seems to want to take quick positions in leading shares or stocks with medium- or long-term prospects and hold on to them, which means there is unsatisfied demand pushing up prices," said one broker.
The second most-traded share was Buenaventura's common stock, which accounted for 8.8 percent of total volume.
